chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I said to him, 'Which charity is the most superior?' He said, 'The effort (struggle) of the poor person.'
Have you not heard the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And they prefer (others) before themselves, even though poverty may afflict them'?

key_terms.جُهْدُ الْمُقِلِّ: The effort/struggle of the poor person

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior form of charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the excellence of charity not by its volume but by the degree of self-sacrifice (*juhd al-muqill*), linking it directly to the Quranic virtue of *ithar* (preferring others). This concept is historically rooted in the Ansar’s generosity during the early Medinan period, serving as a normative model for Shia ethical conduct where spiritual merit outweighs material quantity. The narration emphasizes that true piety is measured by the giver's willingness to forgo their own immediate needs for the sake of others.
